## Start with the failure

Repeated persistence is already sufficient if the question is when a regime summary changes. Escalate only if a scientifically necessary relationship is absent.

## Decision routes

- Interactions appear and disappear and maps through both operations matter: test zigzag persistence.
- Scale and density are jointly ordered and neither can be conditioned away: formulate a multiparameter module.
- A fixed interaction scaffold or mesh has smoothly varying weights and diagram trajectories matter: test a vineyard.
- The algebraic transport of feature directions matters beyond visible vines: investigate a vineyard module.

## Candidate fixed scaffolds

A fixed ambient mesh carrying a density or activity field is more plausible for vineyard assumptions than a raw Rips complex whose moving-point distance order can change globally. A fixed interaction scaffold with changing weights is another candidate, but it changes the object being interpreted.

## Baseline and failure modes

Compare every escalation with repeated persistence and ordinary dynamic statistics. Audit correspondence ambiguity, critical-value crossings, computational cost and dependence on the chosen scaffold.

## Interpretation boundary

This page is a method-selection template. It does not claim that vineyards or multiparameter persistence improve swarm analysis. The advanced object is justified only when its extra maps answer the operational question.

The general decision logic is developed in [Week 8](index.qmd). Detailed
vineyard-module transport belongs to the [expert submodule](vineyards-extension.qmd)
and can be skipped for an applied first pass.
